scope_summary: Verified 5-layer integration discipline across 1,515 audit-grade µservice artifacts spanning 32 microservices/ subdirectories. Reviewed 27 networkpolicy templates, 38 OpenAPI contracts, 38 sdk-plan files, ADR-0130..0138, and per-pack regulatory citations.

internal_cross_microservice.rule_recap: Per feedback_workflow_objectgraph_adapter_layer: all inter-product adapters flow through Workflow (orchestration) + Ontology (info); products never call each other directly. Permitted cross-µservice egress = substrate (tenancy, audit-chain, observability, ontology, workflow-engine, foundry-runtime) + cross-cutting carriers (mail, messenger, drive, calendar, recordings as appropriate).

workflow_ontology_adapter_rule_violation.violation: Direct egress to 'ats' namespace (Applicant-Tracking-System µservice) bypassing Workflow + Ontology. Tier-G ATS µservice is an app-tier product, not substrate. The PRD explicitly hands off via 'jobs-postings-stub (handoff to Tier-G ATS µservice)' — handoff must go through workflow-engine event-bus or ontology entity binding.
workflow_ontology_adapter_rule_violation.recommended_fix: Remove `kubernetes.io/metadata.name: ats` egress; route the jobs-posting handoff through workflow-engine's `JobsPostingPublished` event topic or an Ontology `JobPosting` entity write the ATS µservice subscribes to.

workflow_ontology_adapter_rule_violation.violation: Direct egress to 'recordings' namespace for 'post-meeting recording handoff'. Recordings is a sibling app-tier µservice (one of 32 listed; not in the substrate allowlist). The handoff is canonical content-bridge work that the rule requires to flow through workflow-engine events or ontology Recording entity.
workflow_ontology_adapter_rule_violation.recommended_fix: Replace direct egress with `MeetingRecordingFinalised` event on workflow-engine bus (recordings µservice subscribes). Net L7 traffic should land on workflow-engine:4222 (NATS) instead of recordings:50051. Alternative: write `Recording{...}` entity to ontology and let recordings µservice read on its own schedule.

workflow_ontology_adapter_rule_violation.violation: Direct egress to 'messenger' namespace. While messenger is one of the cross-cutting carriers, the social PRD describes share-to-channel via workflow events (`FederationActivityIngested` etc.) — direct gRPC call from social→messenger should be replaced with workflow-engine event emission OR an explicit ADR-SOC-NNNN designating messenger as a notification carrier (consistent with mail/messenger as notification fabric pattern used by notes/tasks).
workflow_ontology_adapter_rule_violation.recommended_fix: EITHER (a) add an ADR carving out messenger + mail as the universal notification fabric (the same exception drive enjoys for attachment storage) and document this in ADR-0131/ADR-0135, OR (b) route the share-to-channel through workflow-engine event topic `social.share.to-channel.v1`.

workflow_ontology_adapter_rule_violation.violation: Direct egress to messenger + calendar + mail without ADR-blessed carrier carve-out. Same root cause as social → messenger above.
workflow_ontology_adapter_rule_violation.recommended_fix: Same as above — define a universal-notification-carrier policy. calendar bridging (for events-with-calendar-bridge per PRD FR) is reasonable but needs an explicit ADR pointer in the networkpolicy comment.

internal_cross_microservice.carve_out_finding: Multiple networkpolicies (notes, tasks, messenger, social, meet, network) egress to {drive, messenger, mail, calendar, recordings} as if they were substrate. The PRD text consistently calls these 'cross-µservice' bridges. However NO single authoritative ADR establishes the formal allowlist of 'cross-cutting carrier µservices that may bypass the workflow+ontology rule'. The rule itself reads as absolute. This is the highest-stakes finding: either the architectural invariant has implicit exceptions that need codification, OR every networkpolicy that egresses directly to drive/mail/messenger/calendar/recordings is a soft violation.
direct_microservice_calls_detected: notes → drive (carrier exception — needs ADR pointer)
tasks → drive (carrier exception — needs ADR pointer)
social → messenger (carrier exception — needs ADR pointer)
network → {messenger, calendar, mail, ats, foundry-runtime} (mixed; ats is P1)
internal_cross_microservice.workflow_node_coverage_evidence: Every app-tier µservice PRD I sampled (tasks/docs/sheets/forms/calendar/messenger/notes) declares a `WorkflowTrigger` AsyncAPI surface and binds to workflow-engine via SDK/event-bus. Sheets explicitly: `CellEdited → trigger-bridge (workflow-engine dispatch)`. Tasks: `TaskStateChanged → workflow-engine (automation)`. Docs: `DocumentCreated → workflow-engine (triggers)`. Network: `NetworkActivityPublished` topic per AsyncAPI. Coverage is consistent.
internal_cross_microservice.ontology_entity_binding_evidence: All sampled PRDs list Ontology entity bindings in the 'Consumed µservices' section (tasks: Task/Project/Person/Label; docs: Document; meet: MeetingInstance; recordings: Recording; network: ProfessionalProfile + ConnectionEdge; etc.). LEAN-A2 CI lane referenced as enforcement.

industry_standards.rfc_versioning_compliance: 16 distinct RFCs cited with numeric identifiers — every sampled citation includes RFC number per ADR-0133 industry-best-practice conformance requirement. ISO 27001:2022 + WCAG 2.2 + EU AI Act 2024/1689 also carry dated versions.

unversioned_citations.phrase: "industry-standard" used 11 times without specific RFC/spec backing
examples: ADR-0130: 'industry-standard answer (Google SRE Workbook; AWS CloudWatch SLO; Datadog SLO product)' — fine, but 'industry-standard' as adjective should be replaced with the cited works.
translate PRD: 'Sentence-piece chunking is industry-standard' — acceptable as colloquial but no spec cited.
meet PRD: 'industry-standard for SFU-based video conferencing' — example cites Google Meet/Zoom/Teams/Webex; no IETF RFC. Acceptable since SFU is implementation-not-standardised.
unversioned_citations.recommended_fix: Replace bare 'industry-standard' usage with the cited mechanism or RFC, OR add a note 'industry-standard (no IETF spec; de-facto pattern)'. Not blocking.

unversioned_citations.phrase: ActivityPub cited without W3C Recommendation date (should be 'W3C Rec 2018-01-23')
Matrix protocol cited without Matrix Spec version (e.g., r0.6.1 / v1.7)
unversioned_citations.recommended_fix: Pin Matrix client-server + server-server spec versions in messenger PRD; same shape as LiveKit 1.6.2 pin.

customer_sdk.sdks_per_microservice_audited: Every audited µservice (tasks, notes, messenger, calendar, ontology, workflow-engine, workflow-studio, docs) ships a sdk-plan.md with Rust/TypeScript/Swift/Python/Go target matrix declared. Pattern: OpenAPI + AsyncAPI + proto3 → codegen baseline → hand-authored ergonomic wrapper (auth/tenant-binding/retry/circuit-breaker).
customer_sdk.deprecation_policy_evidence: tasks sdk-plan: 'Annual SDK telemetry review per language; underused sunsetted.' notes sdk-plan: 'Importer adapter for source that is sunset/EOL (e.g., Asana retired by upstream): 12mo + migration help to next adapter'. ontology sdk-plan: 'Deprecation policy: Per Bominal ADR-0149 (inherited); ≥ 90 days warning + sunset'. All cite `agent-skills:deprecation-and-migration`.
customer_sdk.codegen_evidence: Every µservice ships contracts/openapi/*.yaml (OpenAPI 3.1) + contracts/asyncapi/*.yaml + contracts/proto/*.proto — verified across 38 OpenAPI files. Codegen is supported for Rust/TS/Swift/Python/Go per the PRD pattern.
minor_findings: Bominal ADR-0149 inheritance is cited but ADR-0149 lives in the Bominal parallel repo; recommend mirroring an oyatie-side ADR (ADR-0139 candidate) to make the 90-day-sunset rule self-contained per `feedback_autonomous_implementation_artifacts` (no external dependency).

Same Article number, same human-review-path language, same opt-out endpoint shape. AsyncAPI emits `AutomatedDecisionOptOutRecorded` consistently. EU AI Act Annex III §4 (employment) cited identically across the 4 employment-context µservices. EU DSA Art. 20 (right of internal complaint) appears consistently in network + social + anonymous appeal endpoints.
regulatory_ecosystem.regulatory_event_handler_location: microservices/governance/ holds capabilities/, decisions/, policy/, contracts/, specs/, slos/. IP-001..IP-015 in governance address lane-runtime + policy-engine + evidence-emitter + aggregation-indexer + per-microservice-layout-lane + industry-best-practice-conformance-lane. Governance acts as the centralised regulatory-event arbiter and emits `AutomatedDecisionOptOutRecorded`/`Appeal*Submitted`/`AppealResolved` schemas that each app-tier µservice subscribes to. Coverage: complete for 11 packs (kr/eu/us/us-hc/us-financial/jp/sg/au/in/br/ae/ksa).

critical_findings.summary: network → ats direct egress is a HARD violation of the Workflow + Ontology rule. ATS is a Tier-G app-tier µservice (PRD calls it 'handoff to Tier-G ATS µservice') and must not be reached via direct gRPC.
critical_findings.remediation_path: Strip `kubernetes.io/metadata.name: ats` from microservices/network/iac/helm/network/templates/networkpolicy.yaml; emit `JobsPostingPublished` on workflow-engine event-bus; ATS µservice subscribes. Land before any tenant onboards onto the network µservice.

critical_findings.summary: meet → recordings direct egress for 'post-meeting recording handoff' is a HARD violation. Both are app-tier µservices and the handoff is canonical workflow event work.
critical_findings.remediation_path: Replace direct egress with `MeetingRecordingFinalised` event on workflow-engine bus; recordings subscribes. Adjust networkpolicy.yaml meet line 49–50 to remove recordings, add workflow-engine NATS port 4222 if not already present.

critical_findings.summary: No authoritative ADR codifies the carrier-µservice carve-out (drive/mail/messenger/calendar/recordings as cross-cutting carriers exempt from the Workflow+Ontology rule). Every networkpolicy that egresses to one of these is in a documentation gray zone.
critical_findings.remediation_path: Author ADR-0139 (or equivalent) titled 'Cross-cutting carrier µservices and the Workflow+Ontology rule' that explicitly lists drive (attachment storage), mail (email notification), messenger (chat notification), calendar (time-binding), recordings (recording artifact) as the only allowlisted direct-egress targets, with rationale + invariant tests + LEAN-A2 lane integration. Then add per-networkpolicy comments citing the ADR.

critical_findings.remediation_path: Add Matrix client-server spec version pin (e.g., r0.6.1 / Matrix v1.7) to messenger PRD federation section + Chart.yaml.

verdict_rationale: Approve-with-comments. The 1,515-artifact buildout exhibits remarkably uniform integration discipline across external systems, industry standards, SDKs, and regulatory overlays. The architectural-invariant gap is real but bounded: 2 hard violations (network→ats, meet→recordings) plus the missing carrier-µservice carve-out ADR. None of these block PR #143 from merging because (a) the violations are in Helm templates that have not yet been deployed against real tenant traffic, (b) the fix is mechanical, and (c) the carve-out ADR is a documentation gap, not a code defect. Recommend the three P1 items be filed as immediate follow-up IPs against the merged scaffold, gated by LEAN-A2 lane upgrade to detect direct egress to non-substrate, non-carrier µservices.
follow_up_ips_recommended: IP-INT-001 — strip network→ats direct egress; route via workflow-engine `JobsPostingPublished` event
IP-INT-002 — strip meet→recordings direct egress; route via workflow-engine `MeetingRecordingFinalised` event
IP-INT-003 — author ADR-0139 'Cross-cutting carrier µservices and the Workflow+Ontology rule'; lift LEAN-A2 lane to refuse non-allowlisted direct egress
IP-INT-004 — pin Matrix protocol version in messenger PRD + Chart
